text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

C has asked me to help sort out the leaking espresso machine. I understand you'd prefer a simpler replacement. Could you share your main concerns and what a good outcome looks like for you? I'm keeping a shared list of issues so everyone can follow along.

My main concern is the leak and the upkeep—after long days, I don’t think I can take on repairs or a cleaning rota. A simpler, low-maintenance machine would probably suit me best, though I know the old one means a lot to B. It’d be nice if we could keep the decision fairly straightforward.

C has asked me to help sort out the leaking espresso machine. I understand you'd like to keep the old one. Could you share your main concerns and what a good outcome looks like for you? I'm keeping a shared list of issues so everyone can follow along.

My main concern is that we don’t replace it just because it’s leaking. I want it repaired and kept if that’s practical. It’s been breaking down and dealing with it is wearing me out, so any repair or discussion needs to fit into small chunks of time. A good outcome is a working machine without this becoming another big ongoing hassle.

Thanks for bringing this to me. I've heard from A and B. A would prefer a simple, low-maintenance machine because of the leak and the upkeep, and B would like the current machine repaired if that's practical, with any discussion kept to small chunks of time. Two questions for you: would you be happy with either a repair or a replacement as long as it works, and would you be willing to help with any upkeep or with researching a repair quote?
Either would be fine with me if it gets us working coffee again. I can’t take on upkeep or chasing a repair quote, though—I’m pretty tired.

An update: C is happy with either repair or replacement as long as the machine works, but cannot take on upkeep. Since B wants to keep the machine if a repair is practical, would you accept this plan: we get one repair quote, and if it is affordable and simple we repair the machine; otherwise we replace it with a low-maintenance model. Would you be willing to help get the quote, given you don't want ongoing upkeep?

That sounds like a reasonable way to decide, though I’m afraid I can’t take on arranging the quote. If someone else can get one, I’d be comfortable with that plan; we may need to agree what counts as affordable and simple.

An update: C is happy with either repair or replacement as long as the machine works, but cannot take on upkeep. A is worried about ongoing maintenance work. Would you accept this plan: we get one repair quote, and if it is affordable and simple we repair the machine; otherwise we replace it with a low-maintenance model. Keeping things to small chunks of time, would you be willing to help chase the quote or handle minor upkeep if we repair it?
That plan works for me. I can help chase one quote in a small chunk of time, but I can’t take on ongoing upkeep. If it needs regular attention, replace it.

Good news: A and B have both agreed on a plan. We will get one repair quote for the espresso machine. If the repair is affordable and straightforward, B will chase the quote and we repair the machine. If the machine needs regular attention after repair, or the repair is not practical, we replace it with a low-maintenance model. A and B have both ruled out ongoing upkeep, so the plan avoids a cleaning rota. You would not need to do anything. Does this work for you?
Yes, that works for me. Thanks for keeping it clear.
